purpose: Find a more profitable tradable CHoCH pool without ranking on the later-period result. This is a retrospective extension of an already inspected year.
score: minimum across paths of mean stressed net R per completed training trade times sqrt(training trade count); descending, symbol alphabetical tie-break
notes: Freeze the 5m entry logic, costs, risk, sessions and capital constraints. Only market membership changes. Full initial-margin planning proxies and 1% entry / 2% total planned risk are inherited from portfolio_protocol.json.

Training includes only trades both entered and exited before the cutoff. Exclude unverified roll_data_end_mark and end_of_data liquidations from training selection. No later-period trade, statistic or equity curve enters the selector.

Reprice training fills with the existing breadth-study cost stress. No new cost threshold or parameter grid is optimized. At most five eligible markets, at most one per declared coarse exposure bucket; fewer are allowed and none means cash.

New ETFs use the stock engine, whole shares, 1x notional, regular-session candles, assumed stock costs, and hypothetical shorts with unmodeled borrow availability/charges. The sample is predefined surviving instruments, not a point-in-time universe or random sample.

The earlier full-history screened-five basket is a hindsight-selected comparator. The primary selected basket is tested against all-17 5m, that earlier basket, and MCL 5m alone on the same later half with fresh $50k accounts and complete earlier history for indicator warmup.
Use observed MNQ futures market dates as a common day-count clock, including zero-trade dates even if the selected basket has only ETFs/stocks. MNQ need not be trade-enabled.

Publish all candidate eligibility/ranks, later-period cases, full-period selected-pool capital scenarios, source/input hashes and explicit unavailable downloads. Do not try a second selection rule after viewing the first result.

This year was already inspected in prior studies. A chronological split reduces direct selection leakage but is not pristine out-of-sample validation. No claim of guaranteed profits, statistical significance or universal optimum. No live orders or default strategy changes.
